Ministerium Tuum Imple (2 TIM 4:5)
Love. Serve. Do the best that is possible.
St Paul’s is a mixed 11-19 comprehensive school with specialist training status. We are a thriving and successful Catholic school with an excellent reputation.
The words of St Paul, on which the Mission of the school is based, mean that we are committed to the care of pupils and the success of every pupil in a way that is rooted in the values of the gospel.
We expect pupils to set themselves high standards in their work, their extra-curricular activities and their relationships with others. We challenge them to do so and support them so that they will achieve. We do this to enable them to make the most of the opportunities offered by St Paul's and to lay the foundations of success and personal development.
We are fortunate in having a well equipped, modern school and we are determined that St Paul's will be second to none in the quality of its staff, curriculum and teaching and learning.
We work together with parents to develop the gifts possessed by the children, so that they are prepared to take a place in the adult world confidently.
For information about the process of applying for a place, visit the Admissions page.
Mrs Jo-Anne Hoarty Headteacher

Vision:
At St Paul’s we aim to fulfill our mission by ensuring we "love, serve and do the best that is possible". Within our Careers curriculum this means we aim to ensure all we do is 'meaningful, aspirational and relevant'.
Meaningful
To serve our students by providing them with meaningful careers advice and opportunities to learn so they are as well equipped as possible to be successful. We also aim to serve our community by ensuring our careers advice fits the local context and economic needs of our area.
Aspirational
In order to ensure our students do the best that is possible we aim to ensure our Careers curriculum inspires our students to be aspirational for themselves and their futures beyond St Paul's.
Relevant
To love our students by ensuring al we do for them is relevant to their individual needs and contexts.
The Careers Team:
Laura Palmiero - Head of Careers and Business Employer Engagement
Nicola Parkins and Nicola Honan - Careers Coordinators
For more information about our careers programme please telephone 01908 669735 or contact laura.palmiero@st-pauls.org.uk or nicola.parkins@st-pauls.org.uk.
Our careers programme has the following aims:
To increase access and choice for pupils;
Our programme provides young people with:
Careers programme overview:
A range of specific activities are planned strategically and delivered at appropriate moments during a young person’s time at St Paul’s. Careers education begins in year 7 and then opportunities grow and develop right up to year 13. In Year 10 students undertake two weeks' worth of Work Experience. For more information on this click here.
Key stage 5 students have an opportunity to take part in a week's worth of Work Experience in a sector that is meaningful, aspirational and relevant to them.
The impact of the careers programme is measured through a variety of methods, including pupil, staff and parents surveys. If you have anything specifically you would like to feedback on please contact nicola.parkins@st-pauls.org.uk and/or laura.palmiero@st-pauls.org.uk. The information relating to careers education published on the school website is reviewed annually in July. To see an overview of the types of activities offered please click here.
Information for employers and training providers:
At St Paul’s we are committed to providing our young people with every opportunity to access the world of work and, with this in mind, we welcome employers, industry representatives and training providers to make contact with us to support our pupils in their journey to employability. To find out about the types of activities you could be involved with please click here.
Information for Parents:
All young people at St Paul’s will receive information about careers during their time at the school. We will provide opportunities for them to develop life skills and core competencies that employers value by enabling them to take part in employment and enterprise events and activities. To find out how you can support young people with careers and employability please click here. To find out more about the local labour market including the sectors that currently employ the most people and those that are growing in this region please click here. There are many additional sources of careers advice. To find more information please click here. To find specific information regarding apprenticeships please click here.
Information for Teachers:
In order to prepare our learners for their next step, teachers will focus on providing opportunities for them to develop employability and life skills, such as confidence, creativity and communication skills, as well as our sharp focus on The Learning Talents. Teachers will draw students’ attention to the skills they are acquiring and make links between specific subjects and employment.
Teachers will extend the learning of young people outside of the classroom in order to help them to understand what the true purpose of their learning is (not just to pass exams!). For further information, please contact laura.palmiero@st-pauls.org.uk or nicola.parkins@st-pauls.org.uk
Information for Pupils in Years 7-11:
Your teachers will work with you to help you develop the skills you need for life and employment. You will receive information about placements and work opportunities and will meet people from the world of work, who could help you to acquire the skills needed to be successful in work. You can see the employability skills here.
St Paul’s is committed to help you to realise your potential, so you can do what you love when you leave school. To find out how you can become more employable after education please click here. There are many additional sources of careers advice. To find more information please click here.
Information for Post-16 pupils:
Your tutors, mentors and teachers will be supporting you to develop your ability to demonstrate to universities and employers that you are a suitable candidate. “Mentoring Mondays”, support through the UCAS and apprenticeship application process. You will have a meeting with the Careers Adviser by the end of Year 13. For information about improving your applications to universities and employers, as well as details of useful websites please click here. There are many additional sources of careers advice. To find more information please click here.

Want To Train To Be A Teacher with an 'Outstanding' Provider? The Tommy Flowers SCITT, based at St Paul's Catholic School, has been dedicated to training excellent primary and secondary teachers who will teach in schools across Milton Keynes.
The Tommy Flowers SCITT has been rated as ‘Outstanding’ by Ofsted in a report that described the provider’s course as “exemplary”, “second to none” and “first rate”. Over 500 teachers have successfully completed their teacher training through the Tommy Flowers SCITT’s courses and the vast majority are employed in primary and secondary schools across Milton Keynes.
The Tommy Flowers SCITT is the only provider based in Milton Keynes that is accredited to deliver teacher training beyond 2024. They deliver a range of different courses depending on candidates prior experience:
To find out more about the Tommy Flowers SCITT’s courses, visit their website and sign up for an information evening. Alternatively, email TFSCITT@st-pauls.org.uk or call 01908 669735 ext 320.

St Paul's has a thriving and successful Learning Support Department, Emmaus Student Support, which supports a range of difficulties from specific learning difficulties to moderate learning difficulties, physical difficulties and behaviour. There are also three specialist provisions, delivered in partnership with the local authority, within the Emmaus Student Support Department and mainstream setting. If you'd like to see who works in Emmaus and have a look at our facilities please take a look at our photo booklet here. All requests for admissions for children with an EHCP should come from the Local Authority. Local Authority requests should be sent to EHCPAdmissions@st-pauls.org.uk.
The school is aware that some parents whose children have EHCP plans have received their secondary school allocation and St. Paul’s has not been named. All places have been allocated by the Local Authority. If you are not happy with your allocation, we would advise that you are in touch with SENDIAS 01908 254518. They are an independent advice and support service. The school has no power to admit children outside of the agreed Local Authority processes and parents should pursue any queries with them with the support of SENDIAS.

The Prospectus and How to Apply
Sixth Form Parent Information Evenings
The Prospectus and How to Apply
Additional Opportunities in the Sixth Form
UCAS and Apprenticeship
Alumni and Supporters Network
Share this page
We offer an extensive range of academic and vocational qualifications that provide for a range of learner requirements. It is possible to study both academic and vocational courses if desired. Most Sixth Form students take three Level 3 (A-level or BTEC) courses and the Extended Project Qualification. Entry requirements vary for different qualifications and are outlined in the prospectus and in the supplementary information .
We also offer a one year Bridging Programme designed for ambitious young people who wish to enhance their suite of qualifications before moving on to Level 3 qualifications or apprenticeships. Developed with the help of leading employers and professional bodies, you'll find the technical content and practical approach you'll need to help you stand out from the crowd and prepare for your next steps, whether that's an apprenticeship, employment or further study at Level 3. If you're looking for a Post 16 Level 2 course designed around what today's employers expect choose BTEC Level 2 in Business, Science or Creative Media.
Any student yet to achieve the standard required for GCSE Mathematics or English will have the opportunity to retake these qualifications in the Sixth Form.
Applications to St Paul's Sixth Form are invited from any student because we are an open access sixth form providing education for all young people regardless of faith. For more information on applications please email our Sixth Form Applications Team here.
When and how can I apply?
If you have any questions about applications please email our Sixth Form admissions team here.
If you'd like to get a taste of life in our Sixth Form please watch the video below.

Ministerium Tuum Imple (2 TIM 4:5)
Love. Serve. Do the best that is possible.
St Paul’s is a mixed 11-19 comprehensive school with specialist training status. We are a thriving and successful Catholic school with an excellent reputation.
The words of St Paul, on which the Mission of the school is based, mean that we are committed to the care of pupils and the success of every pupil in a way that is rooted in the values of the gospel.
We expect pupils to set themselves high standards in their work, their extra-curricular activities and their relationships with others. We challenge them to do so and support them so that they will achieve. We do this to enable them to make the most of the opportunities offered by St Paul's and to lay the foundations of success and personal development.
We are fortunate in having a well equipped, modern school and we are determined that St Paul's will be second to none in the quality of its staff, curriculum and teaching and learning.
We work together with parents to develop the gifts possessed by the children, so that they are prepared to take a place in the adult world confidently.
For information about the process of applying for a place, visit the Admissions page.
Mrs Jo-Anne Hoarty Headteacher
